title: Tickets
description: A private support desk inside your server. Members open a ticket with one click, staff claim and resolve it, and a full transcript is delivered when it closes.

commands.name: ticket
commands.summary: Set up and manage your server's support tickets.
commands.description: The `/ticket` command configures the ticket system and gives staff tools to review and manage tickets. Members never need a command: they open tickets with the **Open Ticket** button on the panel that `/ticket setup` posts.
commands.access: Varies: `setup` needs Manage Server, the others need ticket staff access.

subcommands.name: setup
subcommands.summary: Configure tickets and post the Open Ticket panel.
subcommands.description: Posts the support panel in the channel you choose and saves where ticket channels are created, who can handle them and where transcripts go. Run it again at any time to move the panel or change settings.

options.name: panel_channel
options.description: The text channel where the Open Ticket panel is posted.

options.name: category
options.description: The category in which new ticket channels are created.

options.name: support_role
options.description: The role that can see and resolve tickets. It is mentioned when a ticket opens.

options.name: log_channel
options.description: Where ticket events and transcripts are sent. Keeps the existing log channel if you leave it out.

options.name: max_open
options.description: How many tickets one member may have open at once, from 1 to 10. Defaults to 1.

examples.command: /ticket setup panel_channel:#support category:Tickets support_role:@Support log_channel:#ticket-logs max_open:2

notes: Damselette must be able to send messages in the panel channel and manage channels in the category.

subcommands.name: list
subcommands.description: Shows the most recent tickets with their number, status, owner and subject. Open tickets link directly to their channel.
notes: Only you can see the reply.
Up to the 25 most recent matching tickets are shown.

subcommands.name: view
subcommands.summary: View the details of one ticket.
subcommands.description: Displays a ticket's subject, description, owner, who claimed it, when it was opened and, if finished, how it was resolved.

options.name: number
options.description: The ticket number, for example `12` for ticket #0012.

notes: Only you can see the reply.

subcommands.name: close
subcommands.summary: Resolve and close the ticket you are in.
subcommands.description: Marks the current ticket as resolved, sends the transcript to the log channel and to the ticket owner, then deletes the channel after five seconds. It does the same as the **Resolve & Close** button.

options.name: reason
options.description: Resolution notes shared with the member and saved in the log (up to 1000 characters).

examples.command: /ticket close reason:Role issue fixed, enjoy the server!

notes: Run it inside an open ticket channel.

subcommands.name: add
subcommands.summary: Add another member to the current ticket.
subcommands.description: Gives a member access to the ticket channel so they can read and reply, for example a senior moderator or a second person involved in the issue.

options.name: user
options.description: The member to give access to.

notes: Run it inside an open ticket channel.

subcommands.name: remove
subcommands.summary: Remove a member from the current ticket.
subcommands.description: Takes away a member's access to the ticket channel. The person who opened the ticket cannot be removed.
notes: Run it inside an open ticket channel.
**Ticket staff** means anyone with Administrator, anyone with Manage Server, or anyone holding the support role chosen in `/ticket setup`.
